disagreements.topic: Forward multiple at Sep 2027 (14.0x to 15x) and the historical anchor
disagreements.positions: Agent 3 uses 14.0x, agents 2 and 5 use 14.5x, agents 1 and 4 use 15x. All now anchor on 'ex-COVID troughs of 14-16x versus a normal 18-22x'. The CNBC 10-year average of 22.3x was dropped by agent 5 as unverified.
disagreements.resolution: I rebuilt the history myself from Alpha Vantage monthly prices and quarterly adjusted EPS (split-adjusted), using price over the next four quarters' realized EPS (a perfect-foresight forward P/E). For 2011-2019 the median was about 19x, the range about 15-22.6x, and the troughs about 15x (late 2011 and 2012) and 16.7x (Dec 2018). For 2022-2025 the median was about 19x, with a trough of 11.3-13.8x in mid/late 2022, when EPS later surprised far above expectations. So 22.3x is above my reconstructed median of about 19x: treat it as an upper bound, not the norm. Today the stock is about 13.7x NTM consensus, already at the 2022 trough band. 14.0-15x by Sep 2027 is a partial normalisation that still leaves a 20-25% discount to the 19x median. That is the right zone while the AI-agent question is open. No change to the agents' range. The spread between 14x and 15x is worth only about $13/share on $13.3 NTM EPS.
disagreements.evidence: Alpha Vantage TIME_SERIES_MONTHLY_ADJUSTED (BKNG, SPY) and EARNINGS (quarterly reported EPS), retrieved 2026-10-01; my own computation.

disagreements.topic: How much weight agent 5's own-history drawdown backtest deserves
disagreements.positions: Agent 5: in all 17 months since 2005 that sat 25%+ below the trailing 12-month high, BKNG was up 12 months later (median +67%). It keeps P(>=163) at 0.63, above the mean of 0.608, partly on this. It acknowledges the survivorship bias.
disagreements.resolution: Re-run on the same data (monthly adjusted closes): I get 18 of 18 since 2005 (median +155%). But 16 of those months are the 2008-09 crash, the 2010 flash crash, the 2016 and 2020 sell-offs and the 2022 bear market, when SPY was also deep in drawdown and everything rebounded. Starting in 2000 instead, 41 of 60 such months were up, and 2001-02 and 2003-04 had many -50% to -79% outcomes. This is the survivorship problem made concrete. The relevant analogue for today is an idiosyncratic drawdown: SPY is within 1% of its high while BKNG is down 23% on month-end closes (Dec 2025 $212.67 to Sep 2026 $162.91). On month-end closes it does not even meet agent 5's 25% threshold. For BKNG 20%+ below its high with SPY within 10% of its high, BKNG beat SPY over the next 12 months in only 11 of 22 months (about 5 of 8 distinct episodes: wins in 2005, 2010, 2012, 2016 and 2020, losses in 2004 and 2019, 2015 flat). The 2019 Google-scare analogue was about flat (-0.1%) against SPY +8%. Weight: close to zero for the centre of the distribution, at most a small support for the right tail. It does not justify sitting above the mean.
disagreements.evidence: Alpha Vantage monthly adjusted prices for BKNG and SPY since 1999; my own re-run of the screen.

disagreements.positions: All five keep a 20-25% bear case at $118-122 (about 9.5-10.5x reduced EPS) driven by agents (Meta Muse with Expedia, Google AI Mode, OpenAI). Agent 4 adds AI-referral snapshots (booking.com about 294K AI referrals in June; ChatGPT about 0.3% of referrals). Agent 3 notes that the mid-fifties % direct share leaves about 45% of room nights in paid channels.
disagreements.resolution: The overhang is unresolved and headline-driven, and new entrants keep arriving. OpenAI launched 'Dots' personal agents at DevDay on Sep 29, aimed mainly at enterprise. Booking is not shut out. The CEO (Skift, Sep 23) says AI-generated traffic is 'significantly below 1%' of room nights. Booking has an ad deal with OpenAI and a hotel-booking integration in Google AI Mode, and it runs at least five AI initiatives of its own. Its pitch is that trust in payments and data, not building the agent, is the moat. He also conceded the Connected Trip 'does not yet work as advertised'. No metric yet shows lost room nights or rising marketing intensity. Q2 room nights were +5% and marketing 4.7% of GB. So the 20-25% bear weight and the fat left tail are appropriate. Neither side has data that would move them in the next 12 months, apart from Q3/Q4 marketing-efficiency commentary. No change.
disagreements.evidence: Skift, 'Booking CEO: Building the AI Travel Agent Isn't the Hard Part' (Sep 23, 2026); CNBC/Axios on OpenAI Dots (Sep 29-30, 2026); Q2 2026 release.

disagreements.topic: Q3 2026 results inside the 1-month window (agents put it at about 0.65)
disagreements.positions: All five adopted my round-1 figure of about 0.65 (agent 3: 0.65-0.7). Alpha Vantage's calendar lists Oct 27 and Trendlyne Oct 28, both estimates.
disagreements.resolution: Booking announces its earnings-call date almost exactly four weeks ahead: Q3 2024 announced Oct 2 for Oct 30, Q3 2025 Sep 30 for Oct 28, Q1 2026 Mar 31 for Apr 28, Q2 2026 Jul 7 for Aug 4. As of Oct 1, 2026 its PR Newswire feed shows no Q3 2026 notice; the latest release is Aug 26. On that pattern a report on Tue Oct 27 or Wed Oct 28 is now unlikely. The earliest date consistent with four weeks' notice is about Oct 29. Booking reports after the close, so an Oct 30 report misses the window, and Nov 3-5 looks most likely (Tuesday has been the recent slot, and Q2 already slipped a week). I cut P(results reflected in the Oct 30 close) to about 0.35. That removes some event variance and trims both tails of the 1-month ladder. Agent 4's Q3 EPS consensus of $4.49 matches Alpha Vantage.
disagreements.evidence: PR Newswire Booking Holdings feed (checked Oct 1, 2026: latest releases Aug 26, Aug 25, Aug 3 and Jul 7, no Q3 notice); IR release dated Oct 2, 2024 announcing Oct 30, 2024; Sep 30, 2025 release announcing Oct 28, 2025; Alpha Vantage EARNINGS_CALENDAR (Oct 27, estimate, $4.49).

disagreements.topic: Size of the EPS haircut to consensus (2-3%) and Hormuz
disagreements.positions: Agents 1, 2 and 3 cut consensus by 2%, agent 5 by 2.5% and agent 4 by 3%. Agent 4 justifies its 3% with a worse Kalshi Hormuz curve (17% normal by Jan 2027, 48% by Jul 2027).
disagreements.resolution: CNBC reported on Jul 24 that Kalshi gave 47% for normal Hormuz traffic by Jul 2027. Agent 4's 48% for the same date is therefore corroborated and essentially unchanged since before the Q2 report and the current consensus. The near-term odds did fall. But the Q3 guide (room nights +3-5%) already assumed a continuing Middle East drag, and the 33-analyst FY2027 consensus has been flat since then. A 2-3% haircut is a fair skeptic adjustment. The extra 0.5-1% from Hormuz partly double-counts, and the difference is under $2/share. The fact that matters is that the 'lap the Middle East drag in H1 2027' tailwind I listed in round 1 is weaker: it now needs Hormuz to normalise, at about 30-50% odds by mid-2027.
disagreements.evidence: CNBC on Kalshi Hormuz odds (Jul 24, 2026); agent 4's Oct 1 straits.live/Kalshi relay; Alpha Vantage EARNINGS_ESTIMATES (round 1).

disagreements.positions: Agents 1, 2 and 4 are at $198, agent 5 at $191 and agent 3 at $187. The FCF legs range from $190 to $206 on FY2027 FCF of $10.2-10.8B, about 700-705M shares and 7.5-7.75% yields.
disagreements.resolution: The inputs now agree: consensus EPS less 2-3%, about 700M average shares, 14-15x. The spread is all judgment on the multiple, the yield and agent 2's FCF of $10.8B. On LTM FCF of $9.54B and FY2026 EBITDA growth in the high single digits, FY2027 FCF of about $10.4-10.5B is the centre, so agent 2's $10.8B is the high end. My reconciled FV is $194, essentially the mean. No correction is needed.

one_month_reasoning: Lognormal mixture centred at about $164: 35% that Q3 results land in the Oct 30 close (sigma 12.5%) and 65% that they do not (sigma 10.5%, kept wide for AI-agent headline risk such as OpenAI Dots and Muse partnership news). Booking gives four weeks' notice of its call and had announced nothing by Oct 1, so an Oct 27-28 report is now unlikely and early November is the modal date. The result is slightly thinner tails than the agents' mean.
confidence_reason: I leave the 12-month ladder at the round-2 mean. My checks (the multiple history, re-running agent 5's backtest, the AI news flow, the Hormuz odds) confirmed the agents' centre and argued against agent 5's extra upside, but they found no factual error large enough to move it. Note that the round-2 mean is essentially my round-1 ladder, because all five agents converged on it. The only change is to the 1-month ladder: Booking gives four weeks' notice of its call date and had announced nothing by Oct 1, so I cut P(Q3 in window) from about 0.65 to about 0.35. That is a documented pattern (four of four recent quarters), but it is an inference, and the ladder effect is small (under 1pp per strike). Medium, not high.
thesis_break_reason: $120 is about 9.7x consensus FY2027 EPS ($12.37), about 9x NTM at Sep 2027 and about a 12% FCF yield. It sits at the very bottom of the reconstructed history: the only realized-forward multiples near it are the 2022 trough of 11.3-13.8x, and 2011-2019 never went below about 15x. Getting there needs a fundamental break: room nights near zero, or marketing intensity clearly above 4.7% of GB because agents route demand around OTAs, or a deep travel recession. Litigation and the FTC matter cannot do it alone. All five agents sit at $118-124 (mean $120).
key_drivers: Valuation already at the trough: about 13.7x NTM consensus ($12.37 FY2027, flat) against a reconstructed ex-COVID realized-forward median of about 19x. The troughs were about 15x (2011-12), 16.7x (2018) and 11.3-13.8x (2022). A flat multiple plus EPS growth gives about $180 by Sep 2027.
Buybacks: 751.4M shares at Jul 27, 2026, about 22M retired per quarter, $14.5B authorization. The share count shrinks 6-8% a year, so EPS grows mid-teens even on mid-single-digit room nights.

AI-agent overhang (Meta Muse with Expedia, OpenAI Dots launched Sep 29, Google AI Mode): AI traffic is 'significantly below 1%' of room nights. Booking partners with OpenAI (ads) and Google. There are no lost-share numbers yet, so this sets the multiple, not the earnings, and it supports the 20-25% bear case.

Idiosyncratic drawdown: BKNG is about 23% off its high while SPY is at its high. In the 22 such months since 2004, BKNG beat SPY over the next 12 months only half the time. The 'BKNG always recovers' base rate comes from market-wide crashes and does not apply here.
Middle East / Hormuz: Kalshi gives about 47-48% for normal traffic by Jul 2027, so the H1 2027 easy-comparison tailwind is uncertain. It is already in the Q3 guide and the consensus.

fair_value.reason: P/E: NTM EPS at Sep 2027 of about $13.3 (consensus FY2027 $12.37 less 2%, FY2028 about +12.5-13%) x 14.5x = $193, weight 0.6. FCF: FY2027 FCF of about $10.45B over about 700M average diluted shares = about $14.9 at a 7.6% yield = $196, weight 0.4. Blend about $194, less about $1-2 expected legal cost, which leaves about $193-194. The agents' inputs are now corrected and agree (mean $194.4, range $187-198), so the remaining spread is judgment on the multiple and yield. FV is about 19% above spot. Even so, the ladder median of about $178 sits below it because the market need not close the AI discount within 12 months.

summary: After round 2 the five forecasters converged on corrected inputs (FY2027 consensus EPS of $12.37 and about 700M average shares): mean FV $194, P(>= $163) 0.61, median about $178, thesis break $120. They converged largely onto my round-1 ladder, so the agreement is less independent than it looks. My checks confirm the 14-15x Sep-2027 multiple: the reconstructed ex-COVID median is about 19x and today's 13.7x is already at the 2022 trough. They also show that agent 5's 'every big BKNG drawdown recovered' base rate comes from market-wide crashes. For idiosyncratic drawdowns like this one, BKNG beat SPY only about half the time, so I leave the 12-month ladder at the mean rather than tilting up. Q3 results are now more likely in early November than inside the Oct 30 window, because Booking had not given its usual four weeks' notice by Oct 1, so the 1-month ladder is slightly tighter.
